clue.text: Pass by one with Sherlock Holmes initially

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the two words of the name

parts.note: the first letters of the detective's two names

explanation.surface: Someone dies in the presence of the great detective, a nod to the puzzle's Holmes theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass, or pass away, is a gentle way of saying to die, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Shifting pork pie wedged at first in plumbing …

indicators.note: shifting things move about, so the letters are rearranged
at first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A pork pie has been shoved into the pipes, blocking them.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next as one running story.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipework is the system of pipes in a building, the same thing as its plumbing.

clue.text: … ends oddly with A Study in Scarlet getting flushed

indicators.note: in places the study word inside the colour word and the letters that follow it

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in odd positions, the first and third

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work

explanation.surface: Continuing from the clue above, the Holmes novel A Study in Scarlet ends with someone turning red.
explanation.walkthrough: A Study in Scarlet is the first Holmes novel. DEN goes into REDED at its middle, giving RED + DEN + ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be flushed is to have a face that has gone red, so reddened is a synonym.

clue.text: His Last Bow? It has a couple of twists and turns

definitions.text: It has a couple of twists and turns

indicators.note: last asks for only the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: to bow is to bend at the waist

explanation.surface: His Last Bow is a Holmes story, here given a review saying its plot is twisty.
explanation.walkthrough: The story title splits into three working words: His, Last and Bow.
explanation.definitionFit: An S-bend is the doubled curve of pipe under a sink or toilet that traps water, so it twists two ways.

clue.text: Extremists in sect resolve nothing through power

indicators.note: the extremists of each word are its outermost letters, first and last, kept from every word that follows

parts.note: first and last letters of sect
first and last letters of resolve
first and last letters of nothing
first and last letters of through

explanation.surface: Fanatics in a cult find that force settles no argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The words read like a sentence about extremists, but each of the four words from sect to through gives only its two end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength and power are close synonyms for might or force.

clue.text: They can make neat TV sisters

indicators.note: can make suggests one set of letters being turned into something else entirely

explanation.surface: Some performers could pass as a tidy pair of television sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'They', with the rest describing them: people in drag could well make convincing sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-dressers, who wear clothes of the other sex, could plausibly play sisters on screen, so 'They' refers to them.

clue.text: Drains out of Pilsener vat especially

indicators.note: out of means taken from within, so the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: inside these words, after the PILS

explanation.surface: A brewer empties lager from a vat, especially the Pilsener one.
explanation.definitionFit: To enervate is to sap someone's energy, so it drains them of vitality.

clue.text: Former VP, having promoted good causes by the truckload

indicators.note: to promote a letter is to lift it from its place and move it up to the front

parts.note: Al Gore was US vice president under Clinton

explanation.surface: An ex-vice president who has championed worthy causes on a large scale.
explanation.walkthrough: The G of GORE moves to the front of the name: G + AL + ORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore means in great abundance, plentiful enough to fill a truck.

clue.text: Hound story's beginning altered for American banker

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the gathered letters are rearranged
beginning asks for just the first letter of the word it belongs to

explanation.surface: The Hound of the Baskervilles' opening was changed for a US financier.
explanation.walkthrough: A banker in crosswords is often a river, which has banks. Mrs Hudson, Holmes's landlady, fits the theme too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hudson is a river in New York State, and a river is a banker because it flows between banks.

clue.text: Doctor has split pea soup with father

indicators.note: soup suggests ingredients stirred into a mess, so the letters of the word before it are mixed
something that splits another goes into its middle, pushing its letters apart

parts.note: DR is the usual abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A physician shares his split pea soup with a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split pea soup' looks like one dish, but 'split' tells the doctor to part the pea letters and 'soup' tells them to stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is a familiar title for a priest, especially a military chaplain, addressed as Father.

clue.text: "Having shingles is serious" computer returns

indicators.note: returns means coming back, so the brand name is read from its end to its start

explanation.surface: A medical quote warning that the painful rash shingles is serious, with a puzzling mention of a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: Shingles is the disease in the surface but loose pebbles in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is small beach pebbles, so a path covered in shingle has been gravelled.

clue.text: King developed garden site around front of castle. It's used for wishing well

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go about the single letter
developed land has been reworked, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, stands for King George

indicators.note: front of asks for the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A monarch landscapes grounds around a castle, perhaps adding a wishing well.
explanation.walkthrough: The wishing well in the surface is a garden feature; in the definition it is wishing someone well.
explanation.definitionFit: A greetings card carries good wishes for a birthday or occasion, so it is used to wish someone well.

clue.text: We persuade and we led Sherlock to cut hair and restyle

indicators.note: to restyle is to arrange afresh, as a hairdresser does, so the letters are rearranged
cutting the hair word away from the detective's name leaves only its front part

parts.note: a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: A barber's assistants talked a reluctant Holmes into a haircut and a new style.
explanation.walkthrough: Cutting LOCK from SHERLOCK leaves SHER, which is mixed with WE LED. The definition is in the first person: we who persuade are wheedlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheedlers coax and cajole others with flattery, so 'we persuade' describes what they do.

clue.text: Sign of Four: taken aback by reading work

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the numeral is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: reading is one of the three Rs
go means work or function, as in 'does it go?'

explanation.surface: The Sign of Four, a Holmes novel, being recited from in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sign of Four is a Sherlock Holmes novel; here 'Sign' is the definition and 'Four' becomes IV, turned to VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, the virgin.

clue.text: Battle shows soldiers in TA centres getting organised

indicators.note: being organised means being put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged
in places the soldiers inside the other letters

parts.note: the letters of TA centres, organised

explanation.surface: Territorial Army drill halls are being sorted out to host mock battles.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve; here its letters are simply fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Battle re-enactments are staged performances recreating historic fights, so they are shows of battles.

clue.text: Art able to move when through medium of sculpture

indicators.note: letters made to move change their places, so they are rearranged

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: Art can stir emotions when expressed through sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a soft white stone carved for statues, so it is a material sculptors work in.

clue.text: Sailor meets girl at port? That's unusual!

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
port is the left side of a ship, and L is left

explanation.surface: A sailor meeting a girl in harbour is surprising, the clue jokes against the cliché.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meets' and 'at' just join the parts in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormal means departing from the norm, which is what unusual means.

clue.text: A hollow rock thus makes a kind of dome

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing this kind of dome

parts.note: a geode is a hollow rock lined with crystals

explanation.surface: A hollow stone is used to make a dome shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A geodesic dome, made of triangles in a sphere, is the famous design associated with Buckminster Fuller.

clue.text: It's possible to make attractive kitchen company fit island in

indicators.note: in tells us the island abbreviation goes between the other two parts

parts.note: Magnet is a British kitchen retailer
IS is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A sales pitch claiming a kitchen firm can fit an island unit in an attractive way.
explanation.walkthrough: A kitchen island is a free-standing worktop, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be magnetised can be made to attract iron, hence able to be made attractive.

clue.text: Subject of, e.g. Leaving Las Vegas, getting drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the remaining letters are scrambled
leaving means departing, so the abbreviation before it is taken away

explanation.surface: The theme of the film Leaving Las Vegas is a man drinking himself to death.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaving Las Vegas reads as a film title but splits: EG leaves LAS VEGAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A vassal was a feudal tenant who owed allegiance to a lord, so he is a subject.

clue.text: Spells Second Stain with an S

parts.note: to stain is to tint or colour
an S added at the end

explanation.surface: The Holmes story The Second Stain is written with a capital S.
explanation.walkthrough: The Second Stain is a Holmes story; its title splits into S and TINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stints and spells are both periods of time spent on a task or duty.

clue.text: Regularly hasn't tartar or cavities

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the even letters of these words

explanation.surface: Dental advice: someone who brushes regularly has neither plaque nor holes in the teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all about teeth, but the cavities meant are anatomical ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Antra is the plural of antrum, an anatomical cavity such as a sinus in a bone.

clue.text: Doctor Watson, do I detect an exotic tree?

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters that follow are altered

explanation.surface: Holmes's sidekick wonders aloud whether he has spotted a rare foreign tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Watson looks like a name and title together; Doctor is the anagram signal and Watson is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinwood is a tropical tree prized for its glossy timber, so it is an exotic tree.

clue.text: Famous Indian teapot he filled and tipped up

indicators.note: in a down entry, tipping up turns the letters to run bottom to top
a vessel that is filled has something put inside it

parts.note: an urn is a large vessel for tea

explanation.surface: An Indian man fills a teapot and pours it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first prime minister of independent India, a celebrated national figure.

clue.text: They are where a driver might pull into the pit

definitions.text: They are where a driver might pull into the pit

parts.words: where a driver might pull into the pit
parts.note: surface reading: a racing driver pulling into the pits for fuel and tyres
cryptic reading: a golfer's long club hooks the ball off line into a sandy hollow

explanation.walkthrough: In golf a driver is a club and a pull is a shot that veers sideways, so the pit is a bunker on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand traps are bunkers, sandy hollows on a golf course where a badly struck ball can land.

clue.text: Detective hasn't left accommodation

indicators.note: hasn't means is without, so a letter is dropped

explanation.surface: The detective has left his lodgings, perhaps Baker Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Homes are dwellings, places to live, which is what accommodation provides.

clue.text: Adler set about inspector

indicators.note: about suggests being turned around, so the letters are moved into another order

explanation.surface: Irene Adler, Holmes's adversary, sets about a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Irene Adler and Inspector Lestrade are both characters in the Holmes stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Lestrade is the Scotland Yard inspector who often consults Holmes, so he is an example of an inspector.

clue.text: Turn up line written in biro that's well known

indicators.note: to turn the next word is to read it the other way round
something written in a pen goes inside it, so one letter sits within the brand

parts.note: Bic is a famous brand of ballpoint pen; biro is the British word for one

explanation.surface: Someone appears with a line jotted in ballpoint that everyone recognises.
explanation.definitionFit: Public knowledge is what everyone knows, so public can mean widely known or open to all.
